headline: Leptospirosis Admissions Rise as Hospitals Expand Surge Capacity After Flooding
seoTitle: Leptospirosis Admissions Rise After Flooding | FMB News
seoDescription: DOH reported 5,486 leptospirosis cases nationwide through August 26 and 521 patients in Metro Manila as hospitals expand fast lanes and surge capacity after flooding.
deck: DOH hospitals are using fast lanes, referrals and added bed capacity as post-flood leptospirosis admissions increase in Metro Manila and Central Luzon.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Department of Health reported 5,486 leptospirosis cases nationwide from January 4 through August 26, 2026, while 521 patients had been recorded in Metro Manila as of August 27 following weeks of flooding.
James L. Gordon Memorial Hospital in Olongapo City separately announced that it had reached full bed capacity amid rising patient demand, including suspected and confirmed leptospirosis cases.

sections.heading: Hospital response
paragraphs: Thirty-three DOH hospitals in Metro Manila, the Ilocos Region, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon and the Cordillera Administrative Region have activated leptospirosis fast lanes. DOH is also using referral and surge-capacity protocols to prevent individual hospitals from becoming overwhelmed.

sections.heading: Medicine and prevention
paragraphs: DOH had positioned about 3.1 million doxycycline capsules for prophylaxis through its central office and regional health centers. People exposed to floodwater are advised to seek medical consultation so a clinician can determine whether prophylaxis or treatment is appropriate.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The national case total is lower than the same period in 2025, but officials expect hospitalizations to rise after recent floods because leptospirosis symptoms can develop days or weeks after exposure. San Lazaro Hospital was treating 157 leptospirosis patients on August 28, while Manila had recorded 455 cases and 23 deaths for the year.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: DOH expects the post-flood surge to continue in the coming days. Residents who develop fever, muscle pain, headache, jaundice or reduced urination after flood exposure should seek prompt medical assessment.
